thread:
anya: heads up — nightly evals flagged a big quality drop for rwk-7b on the code-gen prompt set after the quant-profile update last night. failing examples went from 2% -> 18% in the regression bucket.
samir: ugh. which profile landed? the new mixed-int8-256 table? :thinking_face:
anya: yeah mixed-int8-256 with the aggressive per-tensor scaling we tested. calib-bot posted the artifact: s3://redwood-nightlies/1823456/quant_profile_v3.json
mike_h: did you repro locally with the same weights + profile?
anya: reproduces on my devbox when forcing int8 runtime. fp16 baseline matches nightly before-change numbers.
jen.l: any specific failure modes? correctness, truncated outputs, or hallucinations?
anya: mostly incorrect function bodies for the code-gen set (off-by-one loops), plus a higher rate of extraneous tokens in summarization small set. examples:

```
input: write a function to merge two sorted lists
expected: correct merge implementation
rwk-7b-int8: returns pseudocode with missing edge-case and wrong indices
rwk-7b-fp16: correct
```

samir: could be calibration bins overflowing for certain layers — we tuned range per-channel aggressively.
eva_r: quick check — is KV cache handling identical between fp16 and int8 runtime? last time we had a mismatch there it looked like hallucinations.
anya: KV handling differs: int8 runtime uses fused cache packing. i'll try running with packing disabled.
calib-bot: nightly-run: eval_id=rwk7b_20260305_01 | code_gen_failures: 18% | summarization_extraneous_tokens: +7% | quant_profile: mixed-int8-256-v3
mike_h: if disabling packing fixes it, then it's a runtime packing bug. else it's calibration table. can you bisect by toggling per-layer quant on/off?
anya: starting quick ablation now: toggling pack=false on runtime...
anya: (10m) pack=false reduces code-gen failures to 3.5% — big win.
jen.l: that pins it to packing. might be a bug in the packing offsets or dtype cast path.
eva_r: what about regression range vs sequence length? pack may be okay for short seq but break at longer sequences.
anya: good point — the failing examples are mostly seq_len ~512.
samir: probable hypothesis: packing logic uses a 32-byte alignment that was assumed for fp16 but int8's kernel expects 16 — misalignment causes read/write corruption at higher seq.
mike_h: let's open an issue on runtime with repro and attach failing input + model artifact. also add a temporary fallback in nightly to skip mixed-int8-256 until we patch.
anya: creating issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/1248 — added logs, failing inputs, and a tiny repro harness.
calib-bot: scheduled job: rollback quant-profile for nightly to mixed-int8-256-v2 at 2026-03-05T03:10Z per @mike_h
jen.l: for postmortem: add a small unit test that runs pack=true/false on seq=512 with a few layers to catch misalignment.
eva_r: also add an eval assertion in nightlies to compare top-k token diffs vs fp16 and alert on >5% regression in code-gen set.
anya: agreed. I'll follow up with a PR for the runtime fix and add the new unit + alert rule.
samir: thanks — nice catch. can we run a quick full night replay with pack=false to confirm no other regressions?
anya: starting replay now, will drop results in this thread when done.
mike_h: ping me if CI flakes — we should block next deploy until a fix or explicit fallback is in place. :thumbsup:
anya: replay finished — pack=false matches baseline across all quick sets. pushing rollback for main nightly channel.
jen.l: closing loop: add retrospective note to eng-ml weekly that quant-profile changes need a short runtime smoke with seq=512 before rollouts.
anya: done — PRs: runtime#1249 (packing alignment fix), nightlies#431 (alert rule + rollback). I'll request reviews.
samir: great work everyone. next step: postmortem draft and cc infra for release gating.
